info.name: OpenFGA ReBAC New Architecture
info.description:
OpenFGA ReBAC Authorization PoC.

Architecture: Application PostgreSQL holds business data (users, clients, projects, structures, zones, audit_events). OpenFGA holds all authorization relationships and the entire Zone hierarchy -- the `zones` table is a metadata mirror only (id, name, parent_type, parent_id): OpenFGA remains the sole source of truth for zone existence, parent, and cycle detection, never the DB row.

A Structure's OpenFGA parent can be either a Project directly (Client -> Project -> Structure, e.g. Argentina) or a Zone at any nesting depth (Client -> Project -> Zone -> ... -> Structure, e.g. India/Emirates/Mexico) -- both coexist in the same system.

No authentication: user identity is supplied directly as a string (e.g. user:parth) to authorization-aware endpoints. There are no auth headers in this collection.

Run scripts/seed_demo.py before the '08 - Demo Scenarios' and '09 - Security Tests' folders -- they assume the India/Emirates/Mexico/Argentina demo data and demo users already exist.

request.description: Creates the business record only. No OpenFGA relationships are written for clients.
Creates the business record AND writes project:<id>#parent@client:<client_id> in OpenFGA.

Hierarchy (parent) is written to OpenFGA only: zone:<id>#parent@project:<parent_id>. `name` is optional and, if given, is mirrored to the `zones` table for lookup -- it plays no part in authorization or hierarchy.
Zone -> Zone recursion: parent_type can be 'zone', supporting arbitrary nesting depth.
Returns {id, name, parent_type, parent_id}. parent_type/parent_id come from OpenFGA; name comes from the zones metadata-mirror table and is null if the zone was created without one.
